Haven Home & Co. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Haven Home & Co. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions for Q&A queue and mute functions.]

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Haven Home & Co.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer; and David Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, which are subject to risks and uncertainties as described in our SEC filings, including our most recent 10-Q and 10-K. Please refer to those for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report Haven Home & Co.'s performance for Q3. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment marked by persistent inflation and shifting consumer patterns.

Let me highlight five key aspects of our performance this quarter. First, sales per square foot reached a robust $458, up 9.2% year-over-year, reflecting our focus on space productivity. Second, our inventory turnover ratio improved to 5.8x for the full year to date, signaling efficient capital use and reduced markdown risks. Third, we're providing clear earnings guidance for Q4 and full-year 2024, balancing holiday tailwinds with disciplined cost control. Fourth, our key strategic initiatives—like store optimization and omnichannel integration—are gaining traction across the board. And fifth, store remodel and renovation plans are accelerating, with meaningful comp uplifts already materializing.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria to provide more details on our financial results.

Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for Q3.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.3 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year, driven by comp-store growth and digital contributions. Gross margin expanded to 39.2%, primarily driven by favorable product mix, markdown discipline, and shrink reduction efforts.

Let me spend some time on one of our most critical productivity metrics: sales per square foot, or SPSF. For those less familiar, SPSF is total net sales divided by average selling square footage, excluding non-revenue areas like stockrooms and offices. It's the gold standard in brick-and-mortar retail for measuring how well we're monetizing our physical space against e-commerce pressures and changing traffic.

In Q3, we achieved $458 in sales per square foot, a strong 9.2% year-over-year increase and our best quarterly showing since 2019 pre-pandemic levels. This beats our full-year 2023 average of $422 and positions us 15% ahead of specialty retail peers—for example, outperforming At Home and Kirkland's in the $380 to $410 range per their recent filings, though high-end players like Williams-Sonoma run higher at around $1,200. Trailing 12-month SPSF stands at $445, up 7.8% YoY, highlighting a durable recovery.

Key drivers included same-store sales contributions, with comp-store SPSF up 8.5%, powered by 4.2% traffic growth—our highest in two years—plus a 3.1% conversion lift to 28.5% and 1.2% higher average unit retail at $89.45. Average basket rose to $212, thanks to bundling 'room-ready' furniture sets and strong performance in our Haven Luxe bedding line, up 22% in comps.

Geographically, results varied: Sunbelt regions—Texas, Florida, Carolinas, 42% of our 285 stores—hit $512 SPSF, up 12.4% YoY, aided by population migration and better weather. Northeast stores, 28% of the portfolio, were at $396, flat YoY due to wet weather and inflation on middle-income homes. Midwest at $441 benefited from back-to-school furniture demand, while West Coast was $428 amid mall vacancies similar to Macy's and Nordstrom Rack challenges.

Category mix was pivotal: Hardlines like furniture and decor, 62% of sales, delivered $682 SPSF, boosted 14% by modular sectionals and space tweaks. Softlines apparel and textiles reached $312, up 6.8%, via localized testing. Impulse items like seasonal decor exceeded $1,200 SPSF in high-velocity endcaps.

Strategic moves propelled this: Our 'Footprint Forge' redesign hit 65 stores, or 22% of the chain, yielding 18% incremental SPSF with design studios boosting dwell time 25% and conversion 11%. We reclaimed 12% square footage for BOPIS, now 18% of sales, enabling denser layouts. AI planogram tools from RetailNext in 180 stores added $22 to SPSF by optimizing top SKUs and lifting turns to 4.8x. RFID pilots in 20 stores cut shrinkage 30%, freeing display space.

On portfolio management, we closed 8 low performers under $350 SPSF, mostly Northeast malls, and opened 5 urban outposts at $720 SPSF. We target blended 2024 SPSF of $475, closing 10-12 more laggards and adding 8-10 Sunbelt sites.

Forward, Q4 guidance includes 6-8% SPSF growth with stable sentiment, though high rates risk big-ticket buys. Our omnichannel—digital now 32% routed via stores—mitigates this, leveraging tactile advantages per Deloitte.

In short, SPSF signals our shift to efficient, experience-driven retail.

Turning to another efficiency metric, inventory turnover ratio. It's COGS divided by average inventory, showing stock cycles—higher means faster sell-through, better capital, less markdown risk in stores.

Full-year-to-date 2024 turnover is 5.8x, up 12% from 5.2x in 2023, with days inventory outstanding at 63 versus 70. Q3 hit 6.4x, above our 6.2x target. This added 120 basis points to margins, avoiding $45 million in markdowns.

By category, apparel and softlines led at 7.2x, up from 6.5x after culling 18% slow SKUs and emphasizing private-label activewear and bedding at 10x turns, now 25% of category sales. Home goods steady at 5.1x with holiday decor strength; decor impulse at higher rates.

Sunbelt stores achieved 6.9x on warm-weather demand in 42% of doors, supporting localized merch via micro-fulfillment. Midwest at 5.2x faced weather hits, addressed by Zebra RFID replenishment. West and Northeast averaged solid gains.

Drivers: AI demand sensing from Blue Yonder across DCs cut forecast errors 28%, trimming safety stock 15% amid Red Sea freight spikes. Vendor-managed inventory with partners covers 40% of goods, adding 0.7x turns. BOPIS up 35% pulled 22% store inventory digitally.

We outpace peers like Macy's 5.1x and Kohl's 4.9x. This freed $280 million cash for remodels and buybacks.

FY2024 guide: 6.2x-6.5x, with RFID full rollout and drone pilots.

Operating expenses were $1.4 billion, representing 60.9% of revenue, reflecting wage and marketing investments offset by efficiencies.

Net income was $180 million, or $1.52 per share.

We generated $320 million in cash flow from operations.

Inventory levels are currently well-balanced at $850 million, supporting turns.

Maintaining a strong balance sheet, we're positioned for growth.

Now, on forward guidance for Q4 ending December 31, 2024, and full FY2024. This assumes resilient consumers, omnichannel momentum, store optimizations, and private label growth amid wage inflation, Red Sea costs, and Conference Board confidence at 108.7.

Q4 net sales: $8.2B-$8.5B, +3-5% YoY, comps 1.5-3.5% with mid-single traffic and flat-to-1% ticket. Brick-and-mortar ~85%, boosted by 150 'Store of the Future' remodels (250 bps comp lift). Digital +12-15%, 10% total, with BOPIS 22%.

Gross margin 38.0-38.5%, +20-70 bps from markdown cuts via AI, private labels at 28%. SG&A 26.5-27.0% with 5.5% wage hikes, marketing 3.8% for Rewards (45M members, 65% transactions). Adjusted op income $950M-$1.025B, EBITDA 12.8-13.3%, EPS $1.45-$1.60 with $500M buybacks (YTD $1.2B at $48 avg).

Inventory ends Q4 $2.8B-$3.0B, flat to -2% per store, turns 5.2x.

Sunbelt comps +4.2%, Northeast/Midwest +0.8% countered by localized assortments. Apparel 4%, home 3%, hardlines 2.5%.

Full FY2024: sales $32.0B-$32.6B (+2.5-4.0%), comps 2-3%, gross 37.8-38.2% (+40 bps shrink cuts), op income $3.35B-$3.50B, EPS $5.20-$5.50. Capex $1.1B, 70% remodels/supply chain, Atlanta micro-DC live.

Key bets: omnichannel BOPIS 28%, Shopify POS cuts stockouts 18%; 'Green Thread' recycled lines; close 25 stores Q1 2025, open 40 urban. Risks: tariffs (35% imports, 60% hedged), unemployment >4.2%. Upside: holiday traffic, private label 30%.

We're returning 50% FCF via dividends (2.8% yield), buybacks.

Next, an update on key strategic initiatives: store fleet optimization, omnichannel, supply chain resilience, personalization, sustainability.

Store fleet: 180 remodels to 'UrbanHub' format (40k sq ft, beauty/home focus), +14% two-year comps, +22% traffic. Closed 45 rural, saving $120M SG&A; plan 25 new Sunbelt hubs, 30 more closures for 10% productivity gain, +150 bps EBITDA.

Omnichannel: e-comm 28% sales (+6 pts), 35% digital via stores. RFID 70% inventory, -40% errors, turns 5.1x. 'Endless Aisle' AR +15% conversion; DoorDash same-day 12% share. Q3 omni $450M, digital margins +220 bps to 42%.

Supply chain: China sourcing to 42%, Mexico/Vietnam up; Reno DC live, +30% throughput, 97% OTD, -$280M excess. Home goods +11% despite apparel softness.

Personalization: UrbanRewards 45M members (+18%), Einstein AI +28% repeats, +16% AOV. VIP suites $150M incremental.

Sustainability: 25% emissions cut, ThredUp refurbished $45M, 35% sustainable softlines.

Q3 comps +4.2%, gross +110 bps to 38.5%, EBITDA $650M +12%. Raised FY24 comps 3-5%, margins +200 bps, FCF $1.2B.

On store remodels: $450M capex FY2024 (+25%), 75 full remodels ($4.2M each, $125/sq ft), 150 refreshes; three-year to 300 by 2026.

Pilots +14.2% comps, +22% traffic, +8% conversion, AUV $520/sq ft, +150 bps EBITDA.

'NextGen 2.0': open zones, AR mirrors, SFS kiosks (BOPIS 20%), AI shelves -30% OOS; LED/HVAC -28% energy, RFID/AI cameras +11% basket.

Sunbelt 40% (TX/FL +5.2% comps), Northeast 30% urban outposts +16% impulse, Midwest/West 30%.

Paired with 50 closures, rightsizing to higher AUV +8%, 12% rent abatements. 3.2-year payback, 22% IRR.

Q4 starts 20 more; investor tour Sept 15 Atlanta.

This concludes financials. Strong balance sheet supports investments.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines.

David Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Maria. This quarter, we launched our expanded Haven Luxe bedding and modular furniture line, which has seen strong uptake with 22% comp growth and contributions to higher AUR and basket sizes. Early feedback highlights the appeal of our room-ready bundles, and we're excited about upcoming launches in sustainable home essentials targeting Gen Z. These align with our high-margin private label push, now over 28% of sales.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Doe (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflationary pressures on your sales?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation has been a headwind, particularly in the Northeast and Midwest where middle-income households felt it most, holding SPSF flat or lower there. However, Sunbelt strength with population growth and our pricing analytics kept overall comps resilient at 5.2%, traffic up 4.2%. Private labels and bundling drove quality transactions, mitigating AUR erosion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith (Morgan Stanley):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Jane. For Q4, we're guiding comps to 1.5% to 3.5%, with mid-single-digit traffic and stable ticket, factoring holiday seasonality and remodel uplifts. Sunbelt should lead at around 4%, apparel and home strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson (JPMorgan):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Mike. We've diversified from China to 42% exposure, ramped Mexico and Vietnam, and our new Reno DC boosts throughput 30% to 97% on-time delivery. AI forecasting and vendor portals cut lead times 10 days, excess inventory down 22%, positioning us well against Red Sea issues.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Brown with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Brown (Barclays):
Impressive inventory turns—how sustainable, and any category risks?

Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer:
Great question, Lisa. 5.8x is sustainable via full RFID, VMI expansion, and omnichannel pull. Apparel leads at 7.2x post-SKU rationalization; home steady. Electronics softer but offset by decor. FY24 guide 6.2-6.5x assumes no major tariffs.

Operator:
[No further questions at this time.]

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy of space-efficient, omnichannel retail. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us. A replay will be available on our investor relations website shortly. Goodbye.
